matrix_completeness.unit_tests_local: tests/test_public_replay_load_scaling_v1.py: 20/20 passed (transform correctness, matrix completeness, ordering/slack invariants) -- does not cover full-duration simulation-to-completion, which is where the defect below manifests

root_cause_analysis.defect: SIM_MAX_STEPS=200_000 and SIM_DRAIN_STEPS=50_000 are hardcoded constants in src/llmserveopt/policy_separation/public_replay_load_scaling_v1.py (evaluate_cell, ~line 322-323), passed to SimulatorConfig(max_steps=SIM_MAX_STEPS, drain_steps=SIM_DRAIN_STEPS). Combined with the base scenario's service_model_kwargs['step_size']=0.001 (inherited unchanged from public_trace_replay_v1, confirmed identical across lambda), this imposes an effective SIMULATED-WALL-CLOCK CEILING of approximately 200-210 seconds, independent of the load factor lambda.
root_cause_analysis.contrast_with_authoritative_harness: The authoritative prior harness (public_trace_replay_v1.evaluate_scenario_policy, line ~327) constructs SimulatorConfig(gpu_configs=..., service_model=...) WITHOUT max_steps/drain_steps overrides, so it uses SimulatorConfig's own defaults (max_steps=None i.e. unbounded; src/llmserveopt/simulator/simulator.py line 53). That is why the prior layer3_checkpoint.jsonl shows ANWG=1.0, num_completed=200/200 for every one of these windows: the original harness runs until natural completion (all arrivals done + drain_steps idle), with no artificial ceiling.
root_cause_analysis.why_lambda1_is_worst_affected: At lambda=1 (identity transform, no compression), the affected windows' real arrival span is used unscaled. The worst case (PUBLIC_TRACE::burstgpt::w0::augmented) spans 34,064 seconds (~9.5h) of real time; only requests arriving in the first ~200-210s of that span (observed: 4-5 of 200 requests) are ever admitted before the simulation halts. This affects all policies identically (confirmed: all 6 P6 + VTC give bit-identical ANWG/completion per affected window at lambda=1), consistent with a shared harness ceiling rather than a policy-specific bug.
root_cause_analysis.why_this_is_not_isolated_to_lambda1: The ceiling is a FIXED real-time budget (~200-210s), not a fixed number of requests or a step count relative to lambda. As lambda grows, the *scaled* arrival span (original_span / lambda) shrinks, so windows fall under the ~200s ceiling at different lambda thresholds depending on their own real-world span. The single worst window (burstgpt::w0, span 34,064s) requires lambda > ~170 to fit under the ceiling -- ABOVE the top of the entire preregistered grid (128) -- so it is corrupted at every single preregistered lambda value in this experiment, not just lambda=1.

corruption_scope_full_grid.definition: a cell is 'incomplete' if num_completed + num_dropped < num_total (200) -- i.e. some requests never arrived/were-processed before the simulation halted, despite status=='success' and no NaN/error being recorded (the corruption is silent with respect to design check #9/#10, which only check for crashes/NaNs, not scientific completeness)
